key_idea: The answer depends only on d, the number of vertices on the r-p path: n + d*(d-1)/2.
sketch: Off-path subtrees and the path-vertex cuts give n sets that coincide for both rootings, and choosing u and v on the path yields the 'middle segment' sets, one extra for each of the C(d,2) pairs. So compute the distance with binary-lifting LCA (BFS order to avoid recursion depth 2e5) and print n + d(d-1)/2 in 64-bit. O((n+q) log n). Verified against a brute force that enumerates all intersections on trees with n<=7. Pitfalls: r=p gives d=1 and answer n; the result needs long long.
